## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and versioning scheme

## Description

Defines the packaging format that makes a tutorial a self-contained, versioned,
testable artifact independent of Dashboard releases: the metadata that
describes a tutorial, the pinned images it runs on, and the validation
manifest used to test it. This format is the contract the tutorial gallery
launches against and the template all curated tutorials are authored to.

## Scope

- Specify the tutorial packaging format covering the three constituents named
  in the strategy: metadata (tutorial identity and journey classification),
  pinned images (the exact workbench/pipeline images a tutorial runs against),
  and a validation manifest (what a test run checks).
- Define versioning rules so a tutorial can be updated and re-tested without a
  Dashboard release.
- Ensure the format supports both tutorial kinds the gallery must launch:
  notebook tutorials (opened as a workbench) and pipeline tutorials (imported
  into a project's Data Science Pipelines instance).
- Produce a worked example of one packaged tutorial exercising the format
  end-to-end, and a validation run that passes/fails deterministically against
  it.
- Review the format with the teams that consume it (gallery implementation
  and tutorial authoring) before it is finalized.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines metadata, pinned-image references,
  and a validation manifest such that a third party can package a tutorial
  from the spec alone.
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be versioned, and its validation
  manifest can be executed with a deterministic pass/fail outcome, without a
  Dashboard release.
- The format demonstrably supports both a notebook-form tutorial and a
  pipeline-form tutorial (exercised by the worked example).
- The specification is reviewed and accepted by the gallery implementation and
  tutorial authoring owners.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) enabling versioned, independently testable tutorials.
  Priority raised to P0 by inheritance: this epic gates all P0 work in the
  strategy (the gallery launch mechanics and every curated tutorial build
  against the format).

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

Adds the tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a curated, in-console surface
where a user browses maintained tutorials and launches one into their own
project with a single click — opening a workbench preloaded with the
tutorial's notebook, or importing the tutorial's pipeline into the project's
Data Science Pipelines instance.

## Scope

- Build the tutorial gallery view in the Dashboard, listing curated tutorials
  from their packaged metadata (title, journey, description).
- Implement one-click launch for notebook tutorials: selecting one opens a
  workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook, using the image
  pinned in the tutorial's packaging.
- Implement one-click launch for pipeline tutorials: selecting one imports the
  pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance.
- Launch mechanics read the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images) — the gallery launches what the format describes; it does not
  hardcode tutorial content.
- Surface launch state/errors to the user (launching, launched, failed with
  reason).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from within a data science project and
  see the curated tutorials with their metadata.
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery opens a workbench in the
  user's project containing the tutorial's notebook, running the image pinned
  by the tutorial's packaging.
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into the
  project's Data Science Pipelines instance, where it is visible and runnable.
- A failed launch surfaces an actionable error to the user instead of failing
  silently.
- The gallery renders and launches correctly against the current release of
  the platform.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into the
  user's project (workbench with notebook, or pipeline import).

# Notebook tutorial content: five core-journey tutorials

## Description

Authors the five notebook-form tutorials of the curated set, covering the
core getting-started journeys delivered as workbench notebooks: first
workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG
app. Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format, versioned,
and tested against the current release.

## Scope

- Author and curate five notebook tutorials:
  1. First workbench — creating and using a workbench.
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — taking a trained model to a first deployment.
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  images, and a validation manifest.
- Test each tutorial end-to-end against the current platform release; record
  the test outcome in the validation manifest.
- Verify each tutorial launches through the tutorial gallery's one-click
  launch into a workbench with its notebook.
- Maintain tutorial content at the functional level the strategy states; the
  narrative, dataset, and code choices per tutorial are authoring decisions
  for this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist, covering first workbench, data prep, first
  training run, first deployment, and first RAG app.
- Every tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest, and carries a version.
- Every tutorial has been executed successfully against the current release,
  with the result recorded in its validation manifest.
- Every tutorial launches from the tutorial gallery into a workbench in the
  user's project with its notebook (one click, pinned image).
- Tutorial content is in English only (localization is out of scope) and
  assumes no intake tooling (community contribution is out of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — six curated, tested tutorials covering the core journeys;
  this epic delivers the five notebook-form tutorials (the sixth, the
  first-pipeline tutorial, is a pipeline-form tutorial delivered separately
  under Data Science Pipelines).

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for two audiences: users who want to browse
and launch tutorials, and contributors who want to add new tutorials to the
gallery. Produced through the Red Hat docs content process after the
implementation work lands, so the documentation describes what was actually
built.

## Scope

- Author a using-the-gallery documentation topic: what the tutorial gallery
  is, how to browse it from a project, and how to launch a notebook tutorial
  into a workbench or import a pipeline tutorial.
- Author a contribution-process documentation topic: how a new tutorial is
  authored, packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest), tested, and submitted for curation. Per the
  strategy's out-of-scope list, this documents the process only — no
  submission tooling is described as available this release.
- Content outline (inside Scope, per artifact contract):
  1. Getting started with the tutorial gallery (user topic).
  2. Launching a tutorial into your project (user topic).
  3. Contributing a new tutorial (contributor topic: authoring, packaging,
     testing, curation review).
- Technically review the topics against the shipped gallery and tutorial
  packaging implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery,
  including launching notebook and pipeline tutorials.
- A published documentation topic covers the contribution process for new
  tutorials, accurate to the packaging format and curation flow as
  implemented.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implementation
  (gallery behavior, packaging format, contribution process) and review
  comments are resolved.
- The documentation does not describe contribution-submission tooling as
  available (out of scope this release) and is English-only (localization out
  of scope).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation covering gallery usage and the tutorial
  contribution process. Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring priority
  exception (strategy priority Major → P1), not inheritance.

## Triage

Not below-threshold: the strategy explicitly spans three architecturally
distinct work streams with different owners and review processes — product
code (Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), authored content (the tested
tutorials themselves), and documentation. Per the Step 0 escape condition for
multiple distinct work streams, full decomposition applies. Not docs-only:
the Dashboard, Notebooks, and Data Science Pipelines components all require
code/content work beyond reference material.

  Warnings).

  tested tutorials), HLR-3 (P1, tutorial packaging format), HLR-4 (P2,

| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The gallery's launch mechanics build against the packaging format: it must read a tutorial's metadata and pinned images to launch it. A format another epic's code builds against is a serial dependency, not a configuration reference. |

| E001, E002, E003, E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | The docs-authoring epic is blocked by every Implementation epic in the strategy; documentation describes what was built. |
| No E002 → E003 / E002 → E004 edge | Rules 14/15 (parallel) | Tutorial content and the gallery live in different repos with no shared build artifacts. The end-to-end "launches from the gallery" verification is expressed as an acceptance criterion on each content epic, not as a DAG edge. |

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted

  assumption to verify. Acceptance criteria below are derived from the HLRs.
- **Team ownership of content authoring is assumed**: the strategy says the
  three work streams have "different owners" without naming them. Notebook

  the RHOAI Pipelines team (component owners author their domain content). If
  a dedicated content/enablement team exists, E003/E004 reassign to it without

- **Cross-cutting component mapping (E001)**: the packaging format is
  consumed by the Dashboard (launch) and both content epics (authoring). Per
  the single-most-relevant-canonical-name rule it is assigned to `Dashboard`
  (the launch-time consumer that must interpret the format); the span is

- **"First deployment" tutorial mapping**: HLR-2's first-deployment journey

  notebook form (launched as a workbench, per HLR-1's launch mechanics), so it

  parallel after the format lands; the "launches from the gallery"

  gallery is available. This is a coordination risk, not a dependency
